record.original_question: Let A be a block of neighboring spins in the ground state of the XXZ spin chain and let ρ_A be the reduced density matrix obtained by tracing out the rest of the chain. The entanglement of the block is measured by the von Neumann entropy S(ρ_A) = -Tr(ρ_A ln ρ_A). In the gapped antiferromagnetic regime Δ < -1, determine analytically the limiting value S(∞) approached by the entropy of a large block as the number of spins in the block tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: The density matrix of the subsystem A obtained by tracing away the B degrees of freedom is ρ_A = Tr_B(ρ_{A&B}). In a seminal paper [19] Bennet, Bernstein, Popescu and Schumacher discovered that the von Neumann entropy of a subsystem A S(ρ_A) = −Tr(ρ_A ln ρ_A) is a measure of entanglement.
In the gapped antiferromagnetic case (∆ < −1) we expect that S(ρ(n)) will tend to a limiting value S(∞) but at this moment the analytic evaluation of this constant is missing.
Open problem: For the XXZ spin chain in the antiferromagnetic region (∆ < −1) calculate the limiting value of the entropy of a subsystem when the number of spins in the block is large.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain on the infinite one-dimensional lattice with Hamiltonian
H = -∑_{j∈ℤ} ( S^x_j S^x_{j+1} + S^y_j S^y_{j+1} + Δ S^z_j S^z_{j+1} ),
where S^{x,y,z}_j = (1/2)σ^{x,y,z}_j are spin-1/2 operators. Assume Δ < -1, the gapped antiferromagnetic regime, and let |ψ⟩ denote a ground state of H with density matrix ρ = |ψ⟩⟨ψ|.

For an integer n ≥ 1, let A_n be a block of n consecutive spins, and define the reduced density matrix ρ(n) = Tr_{A_n^c} ρ obtained by tracing out the spins outside A_n. Define the von Neumann entanglement entropy
S(ρ(n)) = -Tr( ρ(n) ln ρ(n) ).

Because the chain is gapped, S(ρ(n)) tends to a finite limit
S(∞) := lim_{n→∞} S(ρ(n)).

Determine S(∞) analytically as an explicit function of Δ.
artifact.category_tag: entanglement entropy of integrable spin chains
artifact.status_search_result: An analytic expression for the saturation entropy of the gapped antiferromagnetic XXZ chain (Δ < -1) was obtained by R. Weston (2006) for general spin and reproduced by Ercolessi, Evangelisti, and Franchini in their analytical computations on the XYZ chain (which contains the XXZ Δ<-1 regime as a limit). The answer is given in closed form in terms of complete elliptic integrals / Jacobi theta (Klein's elliptic λ) functions of the standard XXZ anisotropy parameter. Hence the problem is considered solved.

status_evidence.title: Essential singularity in the Renyi entanglement entropy of the XYZ spin-1/2 chain
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical expression for the (Renyi and von Neumann) entanglement entropy of the XYZ chain; in the XXZ limit it reproduces Weston's formula for the gapped antiferromagnetic regime.
status_evidence.claim: Closed-form analytic value of S(∞) for XXZ at Δ<-1 is known and matches Weston's earlier result.

status_evidence.title: Correlation Length and Unusual Corrections to the Entanglement Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Provides analytical formulas for the saturation entanglement entropy of XYZ/XXZ chains in their gapped phases in terms of elliptic functions.
status_evidence.claim: The limiting block entropy in the gapped antiferromagnetic XXZ regime has an explicit analytic form.

status_evidence.title: Permutation operators, entanglement entropy, and the XXZ spin chain in the limit Δ→-1+
status_evidence.snippet: Develops analytic methods for entanglement entropy of the XXZ chain near the antiferromagnetic gapped regime.
status_evidence.claim: Analytical computations of XXZ entanglement entropy in the Δ<-1 phase exist.
